introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2023. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators are allowed. Formulae booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

incertitudes: Q11(i) : sur le dessin a main levee, P semble faire environ 60 degres avec l'horizontale alors que l'angle marque 120 degres est trace entre P et la force de 200 N (arc entre les deux). Lecture retenue : 120 degres entre P et la force de 200 N (P a 30 degres au-dessus de l'horizontale), d'ou P = 400 N et Q = 346,4 N. Si l'angle de 120 degres etait entre P et Q, on aurait P = 230,9 N et Q = 115,5 N.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i) If the three forces 200 N, $P$ N and $Q$ N as shown in the diagram above are in equilibrium, find the values of $P$ and $Q$. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reading the diagram.** The $200$ N force acts vertically downwards, $Q$ acts horizontally to the right (the right-angle mark shows that $Q$ is perpendicular to the $200$ N force) and $P$ acts up and to the left. The angle marked $120^\circ$ is between $P$ and the $200$ N force. Measured from the downward vertical, $P$ points $120^\circ$ round, i.e. it makes $180^\circ-120^\circ=60^\circ$ with the upward vertical, or $30^\circ$ above the horizontal (to the left).

**Equilibrium:** the sum of the components in each direction is zero.

Vertically (up positive): $P\sin30^\circ-200=0\ \Rightarrow\ P\times\dfrac12=200\ \Rightarrow\ P=400.$

Horizontally (right positive): $Q-P\cos30^\circ=0\ \Rightarrow\ Q=400\times\dfrac{\sqrt3}2=200\sqrt3\approx346.4.$

Check with Lami's theorem: $\dfrac{P}{\sin90^\circ}=\dfrac{Q}{\sin120^\circ}=\dfrac{200}{\sin150^\circ}$ (each force over the sine of the angle between the other two): $\dfrac{200}{0.5}=400$, so $P=400$ and $Q=400\sin120^\circ=346.4$ ✓.

**$P=400$ N and $Q=200\sqrt3\approx346.4$ N.**
themes: resultant of forces and equilibrium (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii) A force $(3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j)$ N displaces a particle, from a point A with position vector $5\mathbf i+2\mathbf j$ to a point B with position vector $-3\mathbf i+8\mathbf j$. Find the work done by the force in displacing the particle. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Displacement: $\overrightarrow{AB}=\mathbf r_B-\mathbf r_A=(-3\mathbf i+8\mathbf j)-(5\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)=-8\mathbf i+6\mathbf j$ (in metres).

Work done $=\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf d$ (scalar product):

$$W=(3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j)\cdot(-8\mathbf i+6\mathbf j)=3(-8)+(-2)(6)=-24-12=-36.$$

The negative sign means that the force acts against the direction of the displacement.

**Work done $=-36$ J (the force does $36$ J of negative work).**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(iii) A crane lifts a block of mass 5 kg which is at rest from a horizontal ground vertically upward, to a height of 20 m in 4 seconds. Find

(a) the work done against gravity by the crane, *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Work done against gravity $=$ weight $\times$ height $=mgh$.

$$W=5\times10\times20=1000\ \text{J}.$$

**The work done against gravity is $1000$ J.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (iii)(b) the power generated by the crane. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Power $=\dfrac{\text{work done}}{\text{time taken}}$:

$$P=\frac{1000}{4}=250\ \text{W}.$$

**The power generated by the crane is $250$ W.**
